rows.grounds: neuter noun amṛta in accusative singular
compound kaula plus sadbhāva in accusative singular
imperative form of root śru in second person singular
compound adjective kāmakalā plus ātmaka in accusative singular neuter

items.question: What nectar consisting of kāmakalā constitutes the true nature of Kaula that one is urged to hear?
premises: Amṛtaṃ is the object to be heard.
Kaulasadbhāvaṃ names the true nature of Kaula.
items.inference: The verse identifies the nectar to be heard as the true Kaula nature consisting of kāmakalā.
uncertainties: The exact syntactic relation of kaulasadbhāvaṃ to amṛtaṃ is inferred from context.
Kāmakalātmakam is read as modifying amṛtaṃ.
items.plain_english: Hear the nectar, the true nature of Kaula, which consists of kāmakalā.
